themes_detail.label: Sudden Curb Infrastructure Collapse
themes_detail.summary: Curb condition complaints spiked to 12 THIS WEEK, a 500% increase from the 2.0-complaint weekly baseline over the prior 8 weeks, suggesting rapid deterioration of street infrastructure in Greenwich Village/SoHo that warrants immediate investigation into root causes and repair prioritization.
evidence: 12 curb condition complaints last week vs. 2.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 14.14)
Curb Condition marked as high-severity spike with statistical anomaly
Aligns with recurring CB budget request for street maintenance and catch basin cleaning
reporting_angles: Interview DOT about emergency curb repairs in CD102 and whether weather or construction is accelerating decay
Photo/video documentation of specific curb failures affecting pedestrians and deliveries in SoHo/Spring Street corridor

themes_detail.label: Mysterious Litter Basket Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Litter basket complaints exploded to 3 THIS WEEK, a 2300% spike from the 0.1-complaint weekly baseline, indicating either a rapid service gap or a neighborhood cleanliness crisis emerging in Greenwich Village/SoHo.
evidence: 3 litter basket complaints last week vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 8.69)
Litter basket marked as high-severity spike
Aligns with CB's repeated requests for increased sanitation equipment and trash management
reporting_angles: Contact Sanitation Department to determine if baskets were removed, damaged, or if collection frequency dropped in specific blocks
Survey residents about whether litter accumulation is visible; identify which neighborhoods are most affected

themes_detail.label: Root/Sewer/Sidewalk Damage Wave
themes_detail.summary: Root and sewer-related sidewalk complaints peaked at 4 TWO WEEKS AGO, a 1500% increase from the 0.2-complaint weekly baseline, indicating possible underground infrastructure issues affecting pedestrian safety across the district.
evidence: 4 root/sewer/sidewalk complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 8.66)
Root and sewer issues marked as high-severity spike
Aligns with CB's recurring budget request for catch basin cleaning by DEP
reporting_angles: File FOIL request with DEP to identify sewer backups, tree root encroachment, or subsidence reports in CD102
Document specific locations with lifted/cracked sidewalks; interview affected businesses and residents about trip hazards

themes_detail.label: Abandoned Vehicles Accumulating
themes_detail.summary: Abandoned vehicle complaints reached 13 TWO WEEKS AGO, a 316% increase from the 3.1-complaint weekly baseline, suggesting a possible enforcement gap or influx of derelict cars in Greenwich Village/SoHo parking areas.
evidence: 13 abandoned vehicle complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 3.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.87)
Abandoned vehicle marked as high-severity spike
Illegal parking is already the second-largest complaint category in district (950 over 90 days)
reporting_angles: Map the geographic clusters of abandoned vehicle complaints to identify problem blocks
Interview NYPD Tow and Traffic Enforcement about response times and enforcement priorities in SoHo/Greenwich Village

themes_detail.label: Building Code Violations Spiking
themes_detail.summary: Building/use complaints jumped to 9 THIS WEEK, a 620% increase from the 1.2-complaint weekly baseline, potentially signaling unsafe conditions, illegal conversions, or enforcement action in a district with active major development (246 Spring Street ULURP pending).
evidence: 9 building/use complaints last week vs. 1.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 7.11)
Overlaps with CB's recurring budget request for expanded housing inspections and code violation correction programs
Active ULURP at 246 Spring Street suggests development activity may be creating construction-adjacent violations
reporting_angles: File FOIL with HPD to identify which buildings generated the 9 complaints and what violations were cited (illegal units, safety hazards, etc.)
Interview HPD about inspection capacity and whether the 246 Spring Street development or neighborhood conversion activity is driving complaints
